cheng: Quick Q — trying to profile kernel selection + KV cache hot paths on a long seq (16k). Seeing sudden big kernels during cache miss rounds. What nsys flags you recommend to get a clean kernel timeline + NVTX/OSRT events?

alex: Try capturing cuda + nvtx + osrt and use NVTX capture range so you can limit. Example:

```bash
nsys profile -o out/kv_kernels \n  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \n  --capture-range=nvtx \n  --force-overwrite \n  --sample=cpu \n  --sample-period=100us \n  --duration=45s
```

alex: Key notes: --trace=cuda captures kernel launches/driver API, nvtx gives your ranges (use nvtxRangePush/Pop around batches), osrt includes our runtime markers. CPU sampling helps show host-side stalls.

marie: If you can instrument, use cudaProfilerStart/Stop and capture-range=cudaProfilerApi to shrink trace further. For very large runtimes, also try --sample=none to reduce overhead and just rely on NVTX timestamps.

sam: Also limit to the process to avoid other services: add --target-processes all or pass PID via --pid. And set --duration just long enough for the failing scenario.

alex: After capture, open in Nsight Systems UI or run quick summaries:

```bash
nsys stats out/kv_kernels.qdrep
nsys export --output out/kv_kernels.sqlite out/kv_kernels.qdrep
```

alex: Look for long device kernels around KV refill points, check device activity vs host wait. Kernel names + sizes will hint whether we called a different kernel variant (int8 vs fp16/quantized).

marie: Watch out for data transfer spikes — KV cache misses can cause memcpy + kernel combos. Use timeline filtering (CUDA API + kernel) in UI.

infra-bot: started capture job nsys-2026-03-xx for cheng on node gpu-04 (just a friendly log)

cheng: Great — I'll add NVTX ranges around kv cache lookup, batch start/end and re-run. Will share qdrep.

sam: If you hit huge qdrep sizes, try --compress 1 or set --output to a mounted volume. Also consider --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi with cudaProfilerStart/Stop around critical path.

alex: One more: if you're trying to see kernel selection decisions inside our runtime, add NVTX annotations where kernel selection happens (e.g., nvtxRangePushA("select_kernel")) — then you can correlate selection code with actual kernel launches.
